result.title: Permanent and Transient Representations for Continual Reinforcement Learning
result.comment: Accepted at the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
result.summary: Continual Reinforcement Learning (CRL) agents struggle to adapt to new situations while retaining prior knowledge, leading to a stability-plasticity trade-off. One approach to solving this problem is by using complementary learning systems: one for slow, long-term learning and another for quick, transient adaptation. Anand & Precup (2023) instantiated this idea using permanent and transient value functions, but used the same features in both systems. Intuitively, long-term learning should rely more on parametric representations for broad generalization, while transient learning would be best served by non-parametric representations for situation-specific adaptation. In this paper, we explore this idea both theoretically and empirically. By introducing a novel non-parametric approximation for estimating the transient value function in complex tasks, we demonstrate that our method enables online learning and outperforms competitive baselines on image-based tasks and Craftax-Classic, underscoring the effectiveness of our system-level decomposition.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究持续强化学习中的稳定性—可塑性权衡，采用参数化永久价值函数与非参数瞬态价值函数互补的双系统，并为复杂任务提出非参数瞬态估计方法，在图像任务和 Craftax 上验证在线学习效果。
